title_de: 53-Man Roster Prediction Post Training Camp: Wer schafft es in den finalen Roster?
teaser_de: Die Preseason ist vorbei, alle 32 Teams müssen auf 53 Mann reduzieren. Bei den 49ers sind die Roster-Spots auf fast jeder Position hart umkämpft: ein Tipp für den finalen Kader.
title_en: 53-man roster prediction after training camp: who makes the final cut?
teaser_en: The preseason is over and all 32 teams have to cut down to 53. For the 49ers, roster spots are contested at almost every position: a pick for the final roster.
body_en:
The NFL preseason is drawing to a close, and on Sunday evening it's time: all 32 NFL teams have to cut their rosters down to 53 players. For the 49ers, roster spots are hotly contested at almost every position. Training camp and the preseason have left their mark, and now Kyle Shanahan and his coaching staff have to make a lot of tough decisions.

Who makes the 53-man roster? Who will be released or waived? Who lands on the practice squad?

A quick explanation: all players who do not have four accrued seasons are "waived." That means every team has the chance to "claim" (sign) the player before he hits the open market. If a player is claimed, he automatically goes onto the claiming team's 53-man roster, so a roster spot has to be cleared for him. All players without four accrued seasons have to go through the "waiver wire" ("waivers") first before they can be signed to the practice squad.

All players with more than four accrued seasons become free agents immediately.

There has been an important rule change regarding injured reserve in recent years. Teams can place up to two players on IR on or before August 30 and then activate them again after four games. They have to be placed on IR with the status "designated to return." Previously, players first had to be carried on the final roster and could only be placed on IR after that.

### Here is my current 53-man roster prediction:

### Quarterback (3)

Pre-camp prediction: Brock Purdy, Mac Jones (2)

Post-camp prediction: Brock Purdy, Mac Jones, Kurtis Rourke (3)

In the current prediction, the 49ers carry three quarterbacks on the final 53-man roster. Kurtis Rourke earned the roster spot with his performance against the Titans. If he were waived, another team would probably sign him right away.

The only question here: what about Rourke's injury? Is he a candidate for injured reserve?

### Running back (4)

Pre-camp prediction: Christian McCaffrey, Kyle Juszczyk, Jordan James, Kaelon Black

Post-camp prediction: Christian McCaffrey, Kyle Juszczyk, Jordan James, Kaelon Black (4)

PUP: Isaac Guerendo

Practice squad: Sincere McCormick

All four players named above are safe on the 53-man roster. Sincere McCormick made some good plays in the preseason, but it probably won't be enough for the final roster. He is a candidate for the practice squad.

Isaac Guerendo hasn't taken part in a single practice so far and therefore stays on the PUP list. That means he will miss at least four regular-season games.

### Tight end (3)

Pre-camp prediction: George Kittle, Jake Tonges, Luke Farrell (3)

Post-camp prediction: George Kittle, Jake Tonges, Luke Farrell (3)

Practice squad: Brayden Willis, Khalil Dinkins

Before training camp, the only real question mark at this position was George Kittle. Now that he was activated from the PUP list this week, you can assume there won't be any big surprises at tight end.

### Wide receiver (6)

Pre-camp: Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, Demarcus Robinson (6)

Post-camp prediction: Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De'Zhaun Stribling, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, Demarcus Robinson (6)

IR: Christian Kirk (designated to return)

Practice squad: KhaDarel Hodge, Tony Pauline

Before camp, the wide receiver position was extremely deep. Exactly one month later, here we are: Christian Kirk hasn't practiced a single time because of injury so far, and Ricky Pearsall is out for the entire season with his knee injury.

Because of the injuries to Pearsall and Kirk, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing should be as good as certain to make the final roster. There is still a question mark with Cowing, though: he injured his groin in the game against the Chargers. Whether he will be out for an extended period is currently unknown.

### Offensive tackle (5)

Pre-camp prediction: Trent Williams, Colton McKivitz, Enrique Cruz, Vederian Lowe (4)

Post-camp prediction: Trent Williams, Colton McKivitz, Vederian Lowe, Austen Pleasants, Enrique Cruz (5)

Practice squad: Brandon Parker

Trent Williams and Colton McKivitz are locks; behind them, it gets really exciting: will Enrique Cruz make the 53-man roster? What about Austen Pleasants' injury? Will Vederian Lowe land on IR?

Kyle Shanahan said it was an option that Vederian Lowe would land on IR. Lowe injured his ankle in the first practice of camp and hasn't taken part in any practice since. Even if Lowe isn't healthy for Week 1, I don't expect him to land on IR. His high ankle sprain was more than a month ago now; he should actually be back on the field soon.

Offensive line coach Chris Foerster is a big fan of Enrique Cruz. He probably sees him as Trent Williams' long-term successor. He definitely has the athletic tools, but his performances on the field, in camp and in the preseason weren't nearly good enough. We all knew after the draft that Enrique Cruz is a long-term project. But right now it looks like he needs at least two to three years to arrive at the NFL level.

Cruz showed his best performance in the final preseason game against the Raiders. He probably secured his roster spot with it.

Austen Pleasants' situation is complicated by his injury. We currently don't know how long he will be out with his knee injury. A few days ago, Kyle Shanahan said he could probably be back on the practice field in Australia. As things stand, Vederian Lowe will miss Week 1, which means Austen Pleasants will take over his role as swing tackle. In an emergency, Pleasants could also play left guard. His versatility makes him a valuable player for the coaching staff.

### Interior offensive line (5)

Pre-camp: Jake Brendel, Brett Toth, Dominick Puni, Robert Jones, Connor Colby, Carver Willis (6)

Post-camp prediction: Jake Brendel, Brett Toth, Dominick Puni, Connor Colby, Carver Willis (5)

Practice squad: Drake Nugent, Nick Zakelj, Isaac Alarcon (international)

The only small question marks at this position are Robert Jones and Brett Toth. Jones got hurt in the preseason game against the Chargers. How long he will be out is currently unknown. Brett Toth barely practiced throughout training camp because of injury. At the moment, though, he doesn't seem far from practicing with the team again.

In this scenario, I decided to cut Robert Jones. However, I expect him to land back on the active roster after a few other roster moves, provided he is healthy. Jones already has more than four accrued seasons, which is why he will be released rather than waived.

### Defensive tackle (5)

Pre-camp: Osa Odighizuwa, Alfred Collins, CJ West, Gracen Halton (4)

Post-camp prediction: Osa Odighizuwa, Alfred Collins, CJ West, Gracen Halton, James Thompson Jr. (5)

Practice squad: Sebastian Valdez/Bryson Eason (one of them will probably be claimed)

At defensive tackle, the top four are locks. Osa Odighizuwa, Alfred Collins, CJ West and Gracen Halton all have their roster spots locked up.

After a strong camp and a good preseason, Sebastian Valdez as well as undrafted free agents James Thompson Jr. and Bryson Eason all have a real case for the 53-man roster.

But one of the three has managed to separate himself a bit from the other two, and that's James Thompson Jr. In the preseason, Thompson was very strong against the run and created solid push in the pocket against the pass. Since Collins and CJ West are currently still chasing their form a bit and Gracen Halton is currently injured, it would make sense to carry another defensive tackle on the roster. James Thompson Jr. would definitely have earned it.

### Defensive end (5)

Pre-camp prediction: Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Romello Height, Sam Okuayinonu, Keion White (5)

Post-camp prediction: Nick Bosa, Romello Height, Sam Okuayinonu, Keion White (4)

PUP: Mykel Williams

Practice squad: Ogbo Okoronkwo

Nick Bosa, Romello Height, Sam Okuayinonu and Keion White have their roster spots locked up. As things stand, we can assume that Mykel Williams will start the season on the PUP list and therefore miss the first four games. Kyle Shanahan called him a "long shot" for Week 1.

Nick Bosa hasn't practiced for weeks, and Keion White has also been banged up again and again in recent weeks. So it's not unlikely that the 49ers will carry a fifth defensive end on the 53-man roster.

I expect Ogbo Okoronkwo to be released first and then land on the practice squad or the 53-man roster. Because of the question marks surrounding Bosa (knee) and Height (ankle), the 49ers need another defensive end. With 6 pressures and 3 sacks in the preseason, Okoronkwo has definitely shown that he has the quality for the 53-man roster.

### Linebacker (5)

Pre-camp prediction: Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw, Nick Martin, Luke Gifford, Jaden Dugger, Tatum Bethune (6)

Post-camp prediction: Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw, Luke Gifford, Jaden Dugger, Garrett Wallow (5)

IR: Nick Martin

Practice squad: Jalen Graham, Larry Worth III, Deion Jones

The linebacker position is incredibly deep. Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw are locks as starters, and Jaden Dugger probably as the starting SAM linebacker. Garrett Wallow should also be safe on the 53-man roster. At the press conference after the game against the Raiders, Shanahan said Gifford had a "helluva camp." As a core special teamer, Luke Gifford is probably also safe on the active roster, provided his concussion isn't too serious.

Nick Martin can be expected to start the season on injured reserve because of his hamstring injury.

The hardest decision at this position concerns Tatum Bethune. Because of the depth in the linebacker room, things are getting really tight for him. He could be traded in the next few days.

### Cornerback (5)

Pre-camp prediction: Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, Jack Jones, Ephesians Prysock (4)

Post-camp prediction: Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, Jack Jones, Ephesians Prysock, Darrell Luter Jr. (5)

Practice squad: Eli Apple

There probably won't be any surprises at cornerback. Lenoir and Green remain the starters. Jack Jones is the first backup. Rookie Ephesians Prysock played well in the preseason but could land on injured reserve on Monday. Prysock suffered a shoulder injury in the preseason game against the Raiders.

Because of Prysock's injury, Darrell Luter Jr. could make the 53-man roster. Luter had a good game against the Raiders and may have secured his roster spot with it.

### Nickel back (2)

Pre-camp prediction: Upton Stout, Nate Hobbs, Siran Neal (3)

Post-camp prediction: Upton Stout, Siran Neal (2)

Practice squad: Jakob Robinson

Stout is safe as the starter. Siran Neal played strongly as an outside cornerback against the Raiders and should be a lock as a core special teamer.

Nate Hobbs will probably be released because of his injury. If he is healthy again after a few weeks, it's not unlikely that he will then return to the 49ers.

### Safety (3)

Pre-camp prediction: Malik Mustapha, Marques Sigle, Ji'Ayir Brown (3)

Post-camp prediction: Malik Mustapha, Marques Sigle, Ji'Ayir Brown (3)

Sigle and Brown are safe as starters. Despite his injury, Malik Mustapha will probably land on the 53-man roster. When Mustapha can return to practice is currently unclear.

Ashtyn Davis is another option for the final roster. However, his performances weren't consistent enough, which is why he will probably land on the practice squad.

### Special teams (3)

Pre-camp prediction: Eddy Piñeiro, Corliss Waitman, Jon Weeks (3)

Post-camp prediction: Eddy Piñeiro, Corliss Waitman, Jon Weeks (3)

Surprises on special teams are practically ruled out.

It's definitely going to be really exciting over the next few days! The 53-man rosters have to be set by Sunday at 6 p.m. Eastern Time (midnight German time).
